_readme: The ONE place that says which Supabase project each environment belongs to.
Why this file exists: the backup workflow was called 'Backup Production Database' and backed
up QA. Nothing detected that, because 'production' was a word in a filename rather than a
value anyone checked. Every consumer now reads this file: the app's environment guard
(src/lib/environmentContract.ts), the build gate (vite.config.ts), the audit script, and the
backup/restore tooling. Changing a project ref here changes it everywhere, and the checks that
compare a live connection against these refs will fail closed if the two disagree.
A project ref is NOT a secret: it is already in the repository, in .env.qa, and in every
Supabase URL the app builds. It is here so that tooling can refuse to operate on the wrong
project. Credentials are never stored here.
environmentRefs are also the credentials prefix each environment must use, so a production
backup cannot be run with staging secrets by accident: see scripts/lib/environments.mjs.
clusterId is the Postgres cluster fingerprint (pg_control_system().system_identifier). It is
needed because Supabase's pooler rewrites current_user to 'postgres', so the server cannot be
asked which project it is (measured 2026-10-01: current_user = 'postgres', and
current_setting('supabase.project_ref') = NULL). The fingerprint is recorded here on the first
verified run and compared on every later one, so a cluster swap is detected rather than assumed
away.
localEnvFile names the gitignored file a local run may read credentials from: .env.local for
development (the same file, and the same copy-to location, that .env.example documents for it)
and .env.qa for staging. It is null for production on purpose: production's credentials must
come from repository secrets or an explicit export, so that none of them can end up in the
checkout.
kind distinguishes a hosted project from the local Docker stack: "local" means the environment
is this machine's Supabase CLI stack (see docs/LOCAL_DEVELOPMENT.md), localProjectId is the
project id such a build must resolve to, and localStack holds the coordinates tooling uses.
A local environment deliberately has no projectRef: nothing hosted can be named, so the hosted
tooling that verifies a project ref refuses it once more instead of guessing.
A LOCAL production run — one with no CI secret to read — may still supply credentials, but only
from a file OUTSIDE this repository, through scripts/run-with-production-credentials.mjs. That
keeps the rule above intact rather than relaxing it: the intake tool refuses any path that
resolves inside the repository before it reads a byte, so there is nothing for `git add` to
catch, and the backup tooling itself still reads only the process environment.

development.notes: A Supabase stack running in Docker ON THIS MACHINE (Postgres 17, PostgREST, GoTrue, Realtime, Storage) - not a hosted project, which is why projectRef is null and status is not "active". A third hosted project was the original plan and is blocked by Supabase's free plan (limit 2 active projects per member, already spent on staging and production; `supabase projects create` was refused on 2026-10-12). The local stack resolves that without a third project, without pausing staging or production, and with stronger isolation than a hosted development project would give: there is no network path from it to either hosted environment. Hosted tooling therefore still refuses this environment - a target with no project ref cannot be verified, and local data is disposable, so it is not a backup target either. Runbook: docs/LOCAL_DEVELOPMENT.md. The app enforces the same rule from the other side: src/lib/environmentContract.ts refuses a development build whose VITE_SUPABASE_URL is a hosted *.supabase.co URL, and refuses any resolved project id other than localProjectId below.

staging.notes: Named 'Agri-shop-App-QA' in the dashboard and called QA throughout this repository. It is the staging target: the E2E lane, the QA scripts and both local env files use it. It also holds the engineering tooling's own tables (incident_*, impact_*, engineering_memory).

production.notes: Named 'Agrishop APp'. Confirmed as production on 2026-10-01. Runs on the Free plan, which provides no managed backups, no downloadable backups and no PITR. First verified backup + isolated restore completed 2026-10-01; cluster enrolled from that run's manifest. CORRECTED 2026-10-13: this entry used to say production was 'confirmed to hold real business data (1 shop, 4 users, 6 customers, 52 sales)'. The rows exist, but the tenant is the DEMO one — shop 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001 named 'Default Shop', created by the seeding migrations 0009/0018/0026 — and 23 rows are keyed by demo identities with four accounts on demo phone numbers. Whether the 52 sales are a real shop's records is UNKNOWN, not established. Measure it with `npm run audit:production-data`; the owner's options are in docs/PRODUCTION_DATA_POLICY.md §6, and no tool here may clear it.
